name: Northern Dagara
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Northern Dagara (nort2780) is not in the catalog. Glottolog attaches two stress-titled works to it, both by Anttila & Bodomo: the 1996 ROA-169 ms. 'Stress and tone in Dagaare' and the 2009 ACAL 38 paper 'Prosodic Morphology in Dagaare'. Both were already on file from the fleet's Southern/Central Dagaare (sout2789) work; I copied them to ( written) after verifying the origin URLs live (ROA PDF 370789 bytes; lingref 610858 bytes, both HTTP 200) and read them. The 1996 ms. proposes penultimate word stress independent of tone (p. 18, section 2.5), with tonal polarity derived from tone-to-stress attraction; the 2009 paper gives no stress position, arguing only for a bimoraic foot and stating Gur languages have 'little direct evidence for stress' (p. 56, p. 67). Key caveat: both describe Ghanaian Central Dagaare (Bodomo's dialect, Glottolog sout2789 / ISO dga; the paper itself marks 'Central dialect' vs 'Southern dialect' doublets), not Burkina Faso Northern Dagara (dgi). Glottolog's filing under nort2780 looks like a name-based misattachment; the works are relevant to sout2789, where the fleet already cites the 1996 ms. as its stress source. No first-hand Northern Dagara stress statement exists among the items; nothing remains to acquire from this list (priority none for both). all claims come from the PDFs opened, the lingref index page, and the Glottolog languoid pages fetched sources.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Dagara (Wule) is a two-tone language in which, in addition to tone, a stress accent always falls on the first CV syllable of the phonological word, i.e. the root syllable (Dagara words are root + class suffix, so 'first syllable' = Girault's 'voyelle radicale'); stress placement is independent of the H/L tone scheme.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said in the snippets seen.
new_statements.exceptions: None in the snippet ('toujours accentuée'). Girault 1967 likewise says the intensity accent is 'toujours porté par la voyelle radicale' and has an expressive value rather than being optional or accidental.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the 'mot phonologique' (phonological word) in Wule; Girault frames it as the root vowel of lexemes (citation forms). Nakuma 1998 reports the same for both Burkina dialects (wúlé et lòbr): the accent 'frappe toujours la première syllabe du mot' and is used expressively, in contrast with Ghanaian Dagaari/Waali. Note the contrast with Anttila & Bodomo 1996, who argue for penultimate stress in Ghanaian Central Dagaare (sout2789).
new_statements.identity_note: The statement describes the Wule (wúlé) dialect of Burkina Faso Dagara = Northern Dagara nort2780 (ISO dgi); Girault 1967 and Nakuma 1998 extend the same initial/root accent to Lobr, the other nort2780 dialect. new_statements.quote: As for Dagaare, we propose that word stress falls on the penultimate syllable.
new_statements.citation: Anttila, Arto & Adams Bodomo. 1996. Stress and tone in Dagaare. Ms., Stanford University / NTNU, December 29, 1996. Rutgers Optimality Archive ROA-169. https://roa.rutgers.edu/files/169-1296/
new_statements.locator: section 2.5 'Word stress', p. 18 (section spans pp. 17-20); abstract p. 1
new_statements.reading: Fixed penultimate word stress, independent of the lexical H/L tone contrast, argued from segmental asymmetries (Kennedy 1966 primary vs secondary syllable, contrastive length only in the penult, final-CV apocope), lexical-tone attraction to the penult (tonal polarity) and emphatic/nonemphatic pronoun pairs. BUT the language described is Ghanaian Central Dagaare (Bodomo's dialect; Glottolog sout2789 / ISO dga), where the fleet already files this work; it is not a first-hand statement about Burkina Faso Northern Dagara (nort2780 / dgi). For nort2780 it is a sister-variety proxy only, and the 2009 paper by the same authors says Gur languages show 'little direct evidence for stress'. No first-hand Northern Dagara stress statement was found in this sweep (the nort2780 grammars named by the earlier scan — Delplanque 1983/1986, Somé 2003, Mwinlaaru 2017 — are not in the stress-title item list and were not read here).

sources.note: Comparative remark on the Burkina varieties: 'En dàgàrà (wúlé et lòbr), où l'assimilation tonale est pratiquée, l'accentuation est exploitée à des fins expressives, et frappe toujours la première syllabe du mot... En dagaárī et wáálí, par contre, l'accent n'est pas exploité à des fins expressives, mais plutôt mélodiques.' The book itself describes Ghanaian Dagaare (sout2789); the Dagara remark is second-hand for nort2780 but agrees with Somé 1982 and Girault 1967.
